title: Brooks' theorem on chromatic number and maximum degree
statement: Let $G$ be a connected simple graph on a finite, nonempty vertex set that is neither a complete graph nor isomorphic to a cycle of odd length. Then the chromatic number of $G$ is at most its maximum degree, $\chi(G) \le \Delta(G)$.
hypotheses_covered: G is not isomorphic to any odd cycle
G is not the complete graph
replaced:
(Brooks, 1941; proof by Lov\'asz, 1973). \emph{If \texttt{G} is a connected simple graph
and is neither an odd cycle nor a complete graph, then \texttt{$\chi$ $\le$ $\Delta$}.}
